rationale: Trees on the farm itself: the measured livelihood effect lands on the household that adopts.
In-field practices (zai; bunds; conservation tillage) act on the adopter's own plots.
Micro-catchments sit within the field they serve.
Terraces are built on the cultivated slope; downstream flood/sediment effects are a secondary off-site benefit.
Ponds; dams; spate works and tanks are off-field structures whose water reaches users on and beyond the owning farm.
Pooled evidence spanning in-field and structure practices.

Forest restoration does not occur on farmland (Pete 2026-10-07): farmers feel it downstream and at landscape scale (water; flood; microclimate; NTFP access) or as wider societal benefit; never as an on-plot effect.
The buffer takes the field edge (on-farm land and labour) while water-quality and flood benefits accrue downstream.
Wetland works sit outside cropped land; farmer effects are hydrological and downstream.
